description: Prepares a plan for generating its pictures with a generator of your own: it returns the editorial intent of the film (eil.intent/1) and one generation brief per shot (eil.generation-briefs/1). We run no generator and receive no media: you give the briefs to your own. Input: plan; optional sequence and sequence_revision (names for the sequence the intent describes), visual_family (a term for the kind of picture the sequence is made of; the default is a_roll) and house_style (an object, for the briefs). Output: {intent, briefs}. A plan with validation errors is refused with its diagnostics. No AI model runs. We don't keep the plan. Needs an agent key from a Shoot Plan account, and is free up to 3 projects a month. A project is identified by the plan's work id and title; it counts when this tool first makes a finished document for it that month. shoot_plan_allowance says what is left. Over the limit it answers ALLOWANCE_REACHED: do not retry, a new key will not help, tell your human. A fair-use limit also applies: up to 20 finished-document calls for any one project and 60 for the account each month. To count projects we keep, against your account, a one-way fingerprint (hash) of the project's id and title, the month, how many finished documents were made and when, for 13 months after the end of that month. Plans up to 8 MB and 120 calls a minute (5,000 a day).

house_style.description: Optional house style for the briefs.

plan.description: The plan itself: a dpl.plan/1 JSON object (not text inside a string). Call shoot_plan_format for the schema links and an example.

sequence.description: Optional name for the sequence the intent describes.

sequence_revision.description: Optional revision label for that sequence.

visual_family.description: Optional visual family term; the engine lists the ones it knows if yours is not one.
